# R3.7 — Credential-broker dep legs (BL-19: dep-choice ADR + `dpop` verify + `wrapped_long_lived`)

**Ticket:** `docs/tickets/144_R3.7__credential-broker-dep-legs.md`
(seq 7 of 11, Round 3, manifest row 144). **Requirement ids:**
`BL-19`, `DF-S1.13-1`, `DF-S1.13-4`; `R-2.8.3`; ADR-0342 (D2 revisit
trigger — fired), ADR-0032 (`prepare` hook), ADR-0050 C11;
ADR-0359 + ADR-0360 (new). **Base:** `svitali/harnessharness-r3.6` —
the stacked R3.6 tip (operator merges; mergePolicy: OPERATOR).
**Layer:** fixture-verified — real `ring` signatures generated at
test time; never live-attested, no key custody (OQ-170), no

## What

Executes the operator's **HUMAN-H5 disposition (b)**: one vetted
external crypto crate admitted to the workspace by ADR — then lands
the two credential-broker legs the hermetic contract had refused.

**1. ADR-0359 — the dep-choice ADR precedes any manifest edit**
(first commit). `ring =0.17.14` admitted to `hh-secrets` for
asymmetric signature verification (DPoP proofs) plus test-time
fixture signing; `ring::aead`/`ring::rand` reserved for R3.8's AEAD
surface — anything else needs a sibling ADR. Publication evidence:
crates.io `2025-03-11T19:42:03.889273Z` (~19 months before
selection, ≥ 7-day rule met by a wide margin); newest 0.17.x, not
yanked, carries the RUSTSEC-2025-0009/CVE-2025-4432 fix. The
hermetic-deps contract is amended honestly: no vendored tree
(`cargo vendor` ≈ 88 MB / 1,324 files — rejected); lockfile-pinned +
CI `cargo fetch --locked` + warm-cache `cargo build --offline`; a
cold build requires the admitted fetch. `cargo audit`/`cargo vet`
are not installed on the host — the ADR records posture, not a
ran claim. `Cargo.toml` note, both AGENTS.md clauses, README and CI
amended in step.

**2. `dpop` verification — real, fixture-verified** (ADR-0360).
`DpopProof{alg, public_key, signature}` —
`DpopAlg::{Ed25519, Es256}` — verified by
`ring::signature::UnparsedPublicKey` over per-verb
`dpop:v1:<verb>\x1f<fields>` preimages. `bind` pins the bound key as
the content-free `sender_key` coordinate; `mediate`/
`mediate_sentinel`/`mint`/`verify_minted`/`deliver_wrapped` all
require a proof *by that key* over the verb's own preimage — a
foreign key's valid signature refuses, a bound key over foreign
coordinates refuses, an absent/malformed/unverifying proof refuses
`SenderConstraintUnmet` (ADR-0342 D2's fail-closed posture kept; a
`denied` row is durable before every refusal). A byte-level proof
construction, not a JWT — the honest fixture ceiling, never a
live-issuer claim.

**3. `wrapped_long_lived` delivery** (ADR-0360 D4/D5).
`deliver_wrapped` registers the compensating revocation
durable-before-visible: `security.credential.wrapped{wrap_id,
binding_id, destination, sender_key, compensation_plan_id, …}` and
the delivery's `used` row land in one ledger append; the wrapped
value is caller-held, never durable (SV-2). `compensation_plan_id`
is the deterministic idp/1 coordinate of the `RevokeIntent` set
`revoke` produces over the channel's `revocation_path`s — the S2.4
destination machinery is unchanged. `probe_wrapped` is a closed
pure fold — `applied` while the binding lives, `not_applied` once
the compensator ran (LT-05's revoked-wrap leg), `undeterminable`
when no wrap exists. The `isolation ≥ process_sandbox` gate stays at
`bind` (`EnvironmentNotIsolated` below it).

**4. Ledger class table.** `security.credential.wrapped` registered
audit-grade + provenance-mandatory in `hh-ledger` with its lowering;
the credential field set gains `sender_key`/`wrap_id`/
`compensation_plan_id` — all content-free coordinates.

**5. Build memory.** DF-S1.13-1 `DONE` (dated — wire-side proof
presentation noted honestly: `egress.rs` passes `dpop_proof: None`,
so a dpop channel still refuses through mediated egress; the field
exists for a future presentation leg); DF-S1.13-4 `DONE` (dated);
BL-19 `closed`; `R-2.8.3` → `MET-ENGINEERED(DF-S2.4-2)` (the
TLS-transport leg is §5g.4, env-gated, homed on BL-31); ADR re-homing
— ADR-0244 → BL-43 (fired-answered, dated Re-check), ADR-0342/
0359/0360 → BL-42 (partially-fired/quiet conditionals);
`docs/adr/README.md` regenerated via `adr-index.sh`.

## Tests

New battery `crates/hh-secrets/tests/r3_7.rs` — 11 cells covering
both algorithms × all modes: fixture-signed verify green on
`bind`/`mediate`/`mediate_sentinel`/`mint`/`verify_minted`/
`deliver_wrapped`; absent/wrong-context/foreign-key/malformed
proofs refuse `SenderConstraintUnmet` with the `denied` row durable
first; wrap registration durable-before-visible; `probe_wrapped`
`undeterminable` → `applied` → `not_applied` across revoke with the
`RevokeIntent` naming `/_hh/credentials/revoke`; the isolation gate
re-asserted at `bind`. Scoped suites: `hh-secrets` 48/0/0,
`hh-ledger` 223/0/1i, `hh-env` + `hh-embed` all-green (44 result
lines). `cargo fmt --all --check` clean; `clippy --all-targets`
clean on the touched crates; `check-drift` in sync;
`check-removability` all stanzas; `check-backlog` exit 0 (156
sources, 54/66 engineering-closed); `check-build-memory` in the run
record. Full details in `docs/build/runs/R3.7.md`.

## Note for the operator — host environment during this run

The build host's `syspolicyd` was wedged (uninterruptible sleep,
~186 CPU-hours) plus a parallel Bazel build — each freshly-linked
binary's first `exec` blocked ~4 min at 0 CPU, and
`hh-helper`'s 10 s socket-spawn deadline could not be met. One
honest robustness fix rides the PR:
`HH_HELPER_SPAWN_DEADLINE_MS`/`HH_HELPER_CONNECT_DEADLINE_MS` env
overrides in `hh-env/src/helper.rs` (defaults unchanged — the
contract's 10 s/5 s on a healthy host; CI unaffected). With them
set the full removability gate is green.

**No merge — mergePolicy: OPERATOR.**
